proof_skeleton_nl: Encode each tuple by first sorting its coordinates with deterministic tie-breaking, then recording cumulative differences between consecutive sorted values. This partitions K_{m,g} into disjoint chambers indexed by permutations. Inside a fixed chamber, the genus and Kunz conditions are linear in the difference variables. A chamberwise injection from degree g to degree g+1 is then assumed/proved on those encoded chambers. Finally, decode chamberwise and take the disjoint union over all chambers to obtain the global injection on K_{m,g}.

steps.derives: For every positive tuple x in K_{m,g}, there is a unique sorting permutation sigma_x and a unique difference vector e(x) from which x can be reconstructed by cumulative sums. This gives the basic encoding data needed for the chamber decomposition.

The set K_{m,g} splits as a disjoint union of the chambers X_{m,sigma,g} indexed by permutations sigma of {1,...,m-1}. For each fixed sigma, the encoding x -> e(x) is a bijection from X_{m,sigma,g} onto the corresponding encoded set E_{m,sigma,g}. Thus the global problem decomposes into independent sigma-chambers.

Inside any fixed chamber sigma, the total sum condition x_1+...+x_{m-1}=g becomes the weighted degree equation sum_{r=0}^{m-2}(m-1-r)e_r = g by L2, and the Kunz inequalities become a finite linear system in the variables e by L4. Therefore E_{m,sigma,g} and E_{m,sigma,g+1} are exactly the encoded degree-g and degree-(g+1) slices of the same chamberwise constraint system.
For each permutation sigma, apply L5 to obtain an injective chamberwise map I_{m,sigma,g}:E_{m,sigma,g} -> E_{m,sigma,g+1}. This gives a genus-raising injection separately on every encoded chamber.

Using the uniqueness of the sorting permutation and the family of chamberwise injections from A4, L6 constructs a global map J_{m,g}:K_{m,g} -> K_{m,g+1} by: encode x by its chamber label sigma_x and its difference vector e(x), apply the chamberwise map I_{m,sigma_x,g}, and decode back by cumulative sums. The same lemma shows that this piecewise-defined map is well-defined and injective.
Therefore, for the given integers m >= 2 and g >= 0, there exists an injective function J_{m,g} from K_{m,g} to K_{m,g+1}.
steps.trivial_justification: A5 already constructs such a function and proves its injectivity.
